title: Collapsing Star
description: This demonstration shows how a star collapsing will spin faster due to Conservation of Angular Momentum. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Hang the Hoberman sphere from a tall ring stand setup so that it can spin freely and the string hanging out of the bottom is easily accessible. Give the sphere a push to start it slowly spinning.  Pull the string to collapse the sphere and see it spin faster.  Release the string and the sphere will return to its' original size and speed of rotation.
notes: Be careful not to pinch anything in the collapsing sphere.
equipment: Hoberman Sphere, Stand with Coupler or Pole to Hang from Ceiling

title: Supernova
description: This demonstration shows the conservation of momentum involved in supernova explosions.  The balls are dropped with the tennis ball on top of the basketball.  When they hit the floor, it is like the explosion begins.  The top and lightest ball escapes with the highest speed, like the top lightest layer of a collapsing star. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place  the balls on the lab table so they will not roll off. Balance the tennis ball on top of the basketball in the center.  Release the balls and watch them bounce.  The tennis ball will go very high while the basketball does not. If using the kit: choose a clear space without any easily breakable items. Place the smallest ball onto the top of the Exploding Stars stack. Drop the Exploding Stars onto the ground and watch the topmost ball fly off.
notes: Be sure to perform in a high ceiling area or outside. If the tennis ball is not centered it will fly off to the side. Some practice ahead of time helps with this demo.
equipment: Tennis ball, Basketball, Exploding Stars kit

title: LR Circuit
description: This demonstration shows that in an LR circuit, the current lags the voltage by 90 degrees.  The pico scope shows a plot of the voltage across the resistor and the entire circuit.  The voltage across the resistor is proportional to the current in the circuit.  Therefore, it can be seen that the current lags the voltage.
setup: Set the whiteboard on the lab table.  Connect the webcam to the projector and set it up to view the whiteboard from above. Using circuit scribe build the circuit shown above. Connect the function generator to the circuit.  Connect channel A of the pico scope across the resistor and channel B of the pico scope across the whole circuit. Set the function generator to the 1k sine wave range between 3 and 4 on the dial. Open the pico scope software and turn on channel B.  Set both channels to Auto and AC.  Choose 50 micro s per division and 100 kS.  At the bottom of the screen, Trigger should be set to Auto. Turn on the function generator and observe the graph.
notes: Be sure that all the grounds for the pico scope are connected at the same point as the ground for the function generator!
equipment: Circuit Scribe Kit, Whiteboard, Two BNC to Banana Cables, Pico Scope, BK Precision 3010 Function Generator, 2.7 k ohm Resistor, 25 mH Inductor, Demo Computer, Webcam, Ring Stand

title: RC Circuit
description: This demonstration shows charging and discharging characteristics in an RC circuit.  Pasco voltage probe with Capstone or Vernier voltage probe with Logger Pro works really well. One can also use Pico Scope as well. This is what the life sciences and physics majors do in lab in preparing to understand how neurons are modeled as a RC circuit. The engineering majors have been doing cookbook labs, but do something similar, but slightly easier currently. Time permitting, please see the discussion on comparison-based analysis pathway.
setup: Set the whiteboard on the lab table. Connect the webcam to the projector and set it up to view the whiteboard from above. Using circuit scribe build the circuit shown in the first presentation. Do the first demo to show charging and discharging circuit without any measurements. LED will change from red color in one direction of current flow (saying charging capacitor) and blue in other direction of current flow (say discharging capacitor) Change out the resistors and capacitors to show how the timing constant changes Add a POT to the circuit and change the resistance of the circuit to show how the timing constant (RC) plot changes next Connect the function generator (or Pasco signal generator) to the circuit. Connect Pasco voltage sensor across the resistor. Set the function generator (or Pasco signal generator) to the 1 Hz square wave range (or 9 Volts amplitude and 1 Hz square wave for Pasco signal generator).
notes: Be sure that all the grounds for the pico scope/Pasco are connected at the same point as the ground for the function generator!
equipment: Circuit Scribe KitLED Resistor in Circuit Scribe 2-pin connectorCapacitors in Circuit Scribe 2-pin connectorPOT Circuit Scribe (potentiometer)Wires to connect from circuit on dry erase board and measurement tools, LED Resistor in Circuit Scribe 2-pin connector, Capacitors in Circuit Scribe 2-pin connector, POT Circuit Scribe (potentiometer), Wires to connect from circuit on dry erase board and measurement tools, Whiteboard, Measurements of Voltage versus TimePico ScopeOne BNC to Banana CablePico ScopeBK Precision Function GeneratorPasco 850Voltage probeBanana Cables with alligator clipsSignal Generator that can be setup in Capstone, Pico ScopeOne BNC to Banana CablePico ScopeBK Precision Function Generator, One BNC to Banana Cable, Pico Scope, BK Precision Function Generator, Pasco 850Voltage probeBanana Cables with alligator clipsSignal Generator that can be setup in Capstone, Voltage probe, Banana Cables with alligator clips, Signal Generator that can be setup in Capstone, Demo Computer with Pasco Capstone and Pico Scope software, Webcam

title: RLC Circuit and Resonance
description: This demonstration shows resonance in an RLC circuit.  The pico scope shows a plot of the voltage across the resistor which is proportional to the current in the circuit. Therefore, when the maximum amplitude occurs for this, there is resonance.
setup: Set the whiteboard on the lab table. Connect the webcam to the projector and set it up to view the whiteboard from above. Using circuit scribe build the circuit shown above. Connect the function generator to the circuit. Connect channel A of the pico scope across the resistor. Set the function generator to the 1k sine wave range between 3 and 4 on the dial. Open the pico scope software and turn on channel B. Set channel A to Auto and AC. Choose 50 micro s per division and 100 kS. At the bottom of the screen, Trigger should be set to Auto. Turn on the function generator and observe the graph. Turn the dial on the function generator up and down until you see the graph's amplitude rise and then fall.  The maximum amplitude occurs at resonance.
notes: Be sure that all the grounds for the pico scope are connected at the same point as the ground for the function generator!
equipment: Circuit Scribe Kit, Whiteboard, One BNC to Banana Cable, Pico Scope, BK Precision Function Generator, Demo Computer, Webcam, 2.7 k ohm Resistor, 25 mH Inductor, 2.2 nF Capacitor

title: Tuned Resonator
description: This demonstration shows that when an electrical current is sent through a solenoid, it creates a magnetic field.  When that electrical current is sent through at the resonant frequency, it causes the magnet to oscillate.​ * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Hang the spring from the ring stand.  Attach the pendulum mass to the end of the spring.  Attach the magnet to the bottom of the mass.  Align the solenoid below the spring system.  Adjust the height so that the magnet is just above the solenoid.  Set up the webcam with the projector to view the system. Connect the function generator to the solenoid.  Choose the resonant frequency and sine wave. Turn on the function generator.  The spring system oscillates.
notes: This will only work at the resonant frequency.
equipment: Solenoid, Two Banana Cables, Two Alligator Clips, Pasco Function Generator, Ring Stand, Spring, Pendulum Mass, Magnet, Webcam

title: Capacitance and Plate Separation (Large Plate Capacitor)
description: This demonstration shows the effect of plate spacing in a capacitor.  Voltage across two parallel plates declines as the plates converge, and rises as the plates move apart.  Therefore, as plates converge capacitance increases and it decreases as the plates move farther apart. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the equipment on the lab table.  Connect the webcam to the projector system and set it up to view the electroscope.  Set the plates of the capacitor about two centimeters apart. Remove the top plate of the electrophorus.  Rub the fur on the bottom plate of the electrophorus.  Return the top plate to the base and touch the back of the top plate to ground it.  Take the top plate by the insulated handle and touch one of the capacitor plates.  The electroscope will show a voltage across the plates.
notes: None
equipment: Parallel Plate Capacitor, Electroscope, 2 Banana Cables, Ring Stand, Electrophorus, Fur, Webcam

title: Capacitor Energy (C blowing up R)
description: This demonstration clearly shows the energy stored in a capacitor.  A large capacitor is initially charged, then discharged through a resistor causing it to pop and spark.
setup: Place the power supply and grounding plate apparatus on the lab table with the capacitor on the metal grounding plate. The first terminal (closest to the switch) on the grounding plate should be connected to the right side (G) of the switch. Connect the second terminal to the ground of the power supply. Connect the third terminal to the (-) of the power supply. The fourth terminal should be taped to the grounding plate. The fifth terminal should be connected to the (-) side of the capacitor. The sixth terminal should be taped to the grounding plate. The left side of the switch (PS) should be connected to the (+) of the power supply. Connect the center of the switch (C) to the (+) side of the capacitor via a resistor mounted to a yellow banana plug. Once everything is properly connected, make sure the switch is to the right (G) position.  Plug in the power supply and make sure the capacitor is discharged using the plastic pipe and wire between terminals. Place the switch in the left (PS) position and turn on the power supply.  Charge the capacitor up to 3 kV. Turn off the power supply and lift the switch the center position. Touch the switch to the right side (G) to discharge the capacitor through the resistor.  There should be a pop and flash. Use the pipe and wire between terminals to ensure the capacitor is discharged.
notes: Use caution to ensure that this is properly connected. High voltages are used in this demonstration so use caution at all times. Be sure not to touch the capacitor or parts of the system during use.
equipment: kV Power Supply, 0.5MFD Capacitor, Grounding Plate Apparatus, Banana Plugs with Mounted Resistors (Resistors should be in the 10-20 Ohm range), Plastic Pipe for Discharging

title: Dissected Capacitor
description: This demonstration shows what a paper capacitor looks like unrolled.  It visually displays how capacitors are made.
setup: Place the dissected capacitor board on the demo table. The instructor can talk about the construction and parts of a capacitor.
notes: This capacitor is old, but still displays the concept well.
equipment: Dissected Capacitor Board

title: Effect of a Dielectric on a Capacitor
description: This demonstration shows the effect of adding a dielectric to a capacitor.  As a dielectric is added to a capacitor, the voltage decreases and the capacitance increases. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the equipment on the lab table. Connect the webcam to the projector system and set it up to view the electroscope. Set the plates of the capacitor about two centimeters apart. Remove the top plate of the electrophorus. Rub the fur on the bottom plate of the electrophorus. Return the top plate to the base and touch the back of the top plate to ground it. Take the top plate by the insulated handle and touch one of the capacitor plates. The electroscope will show a voltage across the plates. Place a dielectric between the capacitor plates and see the voltage decrease on the electroscope.  Remove the dielectric and the electroscope returns to its original value.
notes: None
equipment: Parallel Plate Capacitor, Electroscope, Two Banana Cables, Dielectric Materials, Electrohorus, Fur, Ring Stand, Webcam

title: Types of Capacitors
description: This demonstration shows the different types and sizes of capacitors all mounted on one board.
setup: Place the Types of Capacitors Board on the Demo Table. The instructor can show the different types and sizes of capacitors.
notes: None
equipment: Types of Capacitors Board

title: Light Bulb Box
description: This demonstration shows principles of series and parallel circuits.  With the box plugged in, all bulbs light and the differences in brightness may be compared.  Bulbs may be loosened or removed to look at how the circuit changes.
setup: Place the board on the demo table. Insert light bulbs in all the sockets.  Make sure they are all the same power rating. Plug in the board to view the bulbs.  Loosen or remove bulbs to see how they others change.
notes: Be careful, bulbs may become warm.
equipment: Light Bulb Box, Six Light Bulbs of the Same Size

title: RC Bulb Box
description: This demonstration shows a basic RC circuit.  A switch is thrown and a capacitor is charged.  One bulb lights initially until the capacitor is fully charged.  A second switch is thrown and the a different bulb lights until the capacitor is drained.
setup: Screw two light bulbs (preferably of the same size) into the bulb box. Place the bulb box on the demo table and plug it in. Throw the switch to charge the capacitor.  Once the bulb is out, throw the other switch to drain the capacitor.
notes: None
equipment: RC Bulb Box, Two Light Bulbs

title: Double Induction Coils with Cathode Ray Tube
description: As AC current is sent through a large inductor coil, the magnetic field produced by the coil changes in direction and magnitude. The cathode ray responds to the changes in magnetic field by moving and twisting with the current.
setup: Plug both the inductor coil and cathode ray tube into their respective power sources. The power source for the coil should be AC power. Make sure the power source for the coil is connected to the AC ports. Turn on the power to the heat gun in the cathode ray tube. Let the cathode ray tube slowly warm up. A small orange glow should be seen inside the tube. Once the glow is seen, turn on the power to the electron beam. A thin green beam should be seen in the tube. Turn on the AC current to the big coil. Move the cathode ray tube around the coil and watch the beam spiral and move.
notes: This demonstration is not currently available. The electron beam in the cathode ray tube may not point directly straight to begin with. Take note of the original position and continue the demonstration as described above.
equipment: Power source for inductor coilCan be PASCO 850 or generator attached to the base of the cart, Can be PASCO 850 or generator attached to the base of the cart, Power source for cathode ray tubeMust be capable of at least 200 volts, Must be capable of at least 200 volts, Inductor coil on rolling cart, Banana cables, Cathode ray tube

title: Faraday Ice Pail
description: ​This demonstration shows the effect of electrostatic induction on a conducting container. It shows that an electric charge enclosed inside a conducting shell induces an equal charge on the shell, and that in an electrically conducting body, the charge resides entirely on the surface of the conductor. It also can demonstrate the principles behind electromagnetic shielding such as employed in the Faraday cage.
setup: Place the equipment on the lab table.  Connect the cage to the electrometer by plugging the black cable into the front of the electrometer.  Connect the Electrometer to the galvanometer by plugging the two pronged end of the galvanometer cable into the output on the back of the electrometer and the two banana plugs into the galvanometer. Connect the webcam to the projector system and set it up to view the electrometer. Set the electrometer's "Multiplier" switch to 100, the "Range" switch to Volts, and the "Meter" switch to Plus.  After about 30s, the meter's needle springs to life. Set the OPERATE switch to OPERATE. Rub the two proof planes together inside the inner cage.   Remove one plane from the cage. The galvanometer indicates the charge on the plane left in the cage by swinging into the negative or positive direction. The instructor then repeats this procedure with the other proof plane. At the end of the demo, please return the OPERATE switch to ZERO CHECK.
notes: None
equipment: Keithley 621 Electrometer, Faraday Ice Pail with Cable, 2 Different Proof Planes, Galvanometer with gray galvanometer cable, Webcam

title: Hula Hoop Flux
description: ​This demonstration shows the concept of flux.
setup: Use the Hula Hoop to demonstrate flux to students.
notes: None
equipment: Hula Hoop

title: No Charge Resides on Inside of Conductor
description: This demonstration shows how charge distributes itself on a conducting sphere.  By charging the sphere and scraping charge off the inside and outside of the sphere then testing with an electroscope, you can see that charge distributes itself on the outside of the sphere only. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the equipment on the lab table.  Connect the webcam to the projector system and set it up to view the electroscope. Touch the conducting sphere with the hole in the top to the Van de Graaff Generator.  Turn on the generator to charge the sphere.  Remove the sphere and set it on the table.  Turn off the VDG and ground it with the grounding sphere.  Rub the proof plane across the outer surface of the sphere.  Bring the proof plane near the electroscope to see it deflect. Touch the proof plane and conducting sphere to ground them. Touch the conducting sphere with the hole in the top to the Van de Graaff Generator.  Turn on the generator to charge the sphere.  Remove the sphere and set it on the table.  Turn off the VDG and ground it with the grounding sphere.  Rub the proof plane across the inner surface of the sphere.  Bring the proof plane near the electroscope and it won't deflect.
notes: Be careful not to touch the outside of the sphere after scraping charge off the inside.
equipment: Van de Graaff Generator, Grounding Sphere, Proof Plane, Electroscope, Sphere with Opening in the Top, Webcam

title: Non-Uniform Charge on a Teardrop
description: This demonstration shows how charge distributes itself on a teardrop shaped conductor.  When the teardrop shaped conductor is charged with the Van de Graaff Generator, the grounding sphere can be used to see longer arcs at the tip of the conductor where more charge has built up. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the Van de Graaff Generator on the lab table.  Set the teardrop shaped conductor with insulating stand on top of the VDG and tape it into place so that it will not fall.  Tape one end of the banana cable on the surface of the teardrop and the other end to the surface of the sphere on the VDG.  Plug in the grounding sphere. Start the VDG and increase the motor speed.  Bring the grounding sphere near various points on the teardrop.  Start close and get farther away to see where the longest arcs occur. Turn off the VDG and ground the system with the grounding sphere.
notes: None
equipment: Van de Graaff Generator, Grounding Sphere (Ovoid Shape), Banana Cable, Electrical Tape

title: Van de Graaff Bells
description: This demonstration shows static electric repulsion.  Two balls coated with conducting paint are suspended between three bells on a stand which is connected to the Van de Graaff generator.  A ball strikes one bell and obtains that charge; it is then repelled by that bell and is attracted to the other one. The ball strikes the other bell, is discharged and obtains the charge of the bell it just struck, thus being repelled again. This sequence soon becomes very rapid and the ball begins to bounce from one bell to the other, ringing the bell.​
setup: Place the Van de Graaff and the bells apparatus on the lab table.  Connect the Van de Graaff and the bells apparatus with the banana cable to ground them.  Tape the red connecting wire to the sphere of the Van de Graaff. Turn on the Van de Graaff and increase the motor speed.  The bells should begin to ring.
notes: None
equipment: Van de Graaff Generator, Bells Apparatus, One Banana Cable, Connecting Wire

title: Van de Graaff Candles
description: This demonstration illustrates the concept of the electric wind.  When the Van de Graaff Generator is turned on, candles near it are blown out.  Candle flames are greatly composed of positive ions which are repelled from the Van de Graaff and help blow out the candle.
setup: Place the Van de Graaff Generator on the demonstration table. Place the stand with candles nearby so that some candles are close and others are farther away from the generator. Light the candles. Turn on the generator and some of the candles will go out, specifically the ones closer to the generator.
notes: Be sure to blow out the candles when demonstration is completed. This can also be done with a small candle on top of the Van de Graaff generator.
equipment: Van de Graaff Generator, Stand with Several Candles, Lighter

title: Van de Graaff Hailstorm
description: When one plate of the hailstorm is charged, the balls are either attracted to it or repelled from it.  Once they hit the opposite plate, they deposite their charge (or gain charge) and fall back to the original plate.  This process repeats if hooked up to the Van de Graaff so there is continuous charge provided.  If a limited charge is placed on the plate, the balls will eventually stop moving.  If the system is grounded, the balls will also stop moving. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the Van de Graaff Generator and the hailstorm apparatus on the table. The hailstorm apparatus  may be connected to the Van de Graaff using the banana cables.  When the hailstorm is charged, the balls will bounce between the plates. Use the grounding wand to ground the system and the balls will stop moving.
notes: None
equipment: Van de Graaff Generator, Grounding Wand, Banana Cables, Electric Tape, Hailstorm Apparatus

title: Van de Graaff Hair
description: This demonstration shows static electric repulsion. As the Van de Graaff generator charges the sphere on top, charge is transferred to the hair. As the charges repel and move as far away from each other as possible, the hair stands up and stretches out. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the Van de Graaff Generator and wig on the lab table.Place the wig on top of the sphere on the Van de Graaff.  Turn on the generator and increase the motor speed using the knob.  After a few moments, the hair will stand up.
notes: This may also be done with a person if they place their hand on the sphere before starting up the generator and they stand on an insulating stool.
equipment: Van de Graaff Generator, Wig

title: Van de Graaff Pie Pans
description: This demonstration shows electrostatic repulsion.  Aluminum pie plates are stacked on top of the Van de Graaff generator. As the plates become charged, static electric repulsion will push the top plate off the stack, causing it to fly through the air. The next plates will follow suit with only a second or so between each plate. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the equipment on the lab table.Put the pie pans upside down on top of the Van de Graaff Generator.  Turn on the generator and increase the motor speed using the dial.  The pie pans will fly off.  Turn off the generator and discharge the top sphere using the discharge sphere.
notes: None
equipment: Van de Graaff Generator, Pie Pans

title: Van de Graaff Pith Ball
description: This demonstration shows electrostatic repulsion.  As the Van de Graaff is charged, the pith ball is charged as well.  As the like charge builds the pith ball is repelled from the Van de Graaff sphere.
setup: Place the Van de Graaff on the lab table.  Tape the pith ball to the top of the sphere. Turn on the Van de Graaff and increase the motor speed.  The pith ball will raise up off the sphere.
notes: None
equipment: Van de Graaff Generator, Pith Ball, Tape

title: Eddy Current Tube
description: This demonstration shows the effect of eddy currents in a copper tube vs. an acrylic tube.  As a magnet falls through each tube, the magnet in the copper tube falls much slower. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Using the ring stand, hang the copper and plastic tubes. Drop the magnets down each tube to see the difference.
notes: None
equipment: Copper Tube, Plastic Tube, Magnets, Ring Stand

title: Electric Motor
description: Electric motors convert electrical energy to mechanical energy.  This demonstration setup has two bar magnets with coils on a post in between them.  When a current runs through the coils (provided by a battery), the post spins from the force of the magnetic field on the moving charges. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the electric motor on the demonstration table.  Connect the wires to the battery in holder using alligator clips. Spin the shaft (or coils) to start the motor. The magnet position may be adjusted to improve performance.
notes: None
equipment: Electric Motor Setup, D Battery in Holder, Two Alligator Clips

title: Giant Earth Inductor
description: This demostration shows the presents of Earth's magnetic field as well as the concept of inductance. When one end of the large exention cord is spun (in a "jump rope" fashion) the EMF induced due to the change in the magnetic field flux in the closed loop can be measured on a galvanometer.
setup: Attatch the two plugs into the ends of the extension cords and place the two banana plug cables into the galvanometer. Lay the extention cable out across the front of the room. Spin one end of the cable to change the area of the enclosed loop. The induced emf can be measured on the galvanometer.
equipment: Long extension cable, 3-prong adapter to banana cable, Galvanometer

title: Hand Crank Generator and Bulb
description: This demonstration shows conversion of mechanical to electrical energy.  When the handle is turned on this simple hand crank generator, the bulb lights up. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the hand crank generator and bulb in socket on the demo table.  Make sure that the bulb is screwed in so it makes a solid connection. Clip the alligator leads onto the bulb socket. Turn the handle on the generator and watch the bulb light up.  The faster the handle is turned, the brighter the bulb gets.
notes: None
equipment: Genecon Hand Crank Generator, Miniature Light Bulb in Socket

title: Hand Crank Generator EMF
description: One generator induces an EMF in a second Genecon as it's crank is turned. The EMF causes the second Genecon, supported by a stand, to behave as a motor. The second Genecon's handle turns.
setup: Use the ring stand to secure one of the hand crank generators.  Connect the wires of the generators. Setup the webcam with the projector to view the generator in the stand. Crank one of the generators and watch the other crank turn.
notes: None
equipment: Two Hand Crank Generators, Ring Stand, Webcam

title: Lenz's Law and the Rolling Rod
description: This demonstration shows eddy currents in an aluminum rod as it rolls in a magnetic field.  When the aluminum rod rolls down the rails and enters the magnetic field it appears to slow down. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup. Optional: * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the apparatus on the lab table.  Connect the webcam to the projector system and set it up to view the apparatus. Place the rod on the rails and release it.  The rod will roll down the rails and slow down when it enters the magnetic field.
notes: If a battery is connected across the rails, the rod will roll back up the ramp once it enters the magnetic field.
equipment: Rail Roll Apparatus with Magnet and Small Rod, Optional:6V BatteryTwo Alligator Cables, 6V Battery, Two Alligator Cables

title: Moving a Magnet through a Coil
description: This setup shows how an electric current can be produced in a coil by moving a magnet.  A magnet is moved into and out of a large coil which induces a current in the coil.  This is visible on the large galvanometer connected to the coil. The sign of the current changes as the direction of the motion changes. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the large galvanometer on the lab table.  Connect the red and black leads of the coil to the red and black jacks in the center of the galvanometer.  Place the strong magnet on the lab table by the coil. Move the magnet into and out of the coil to see the needle on the galvanometer move.  When you move the magnet in the opposite direction, the galvanometer should read the opposite sign.
notes: It takes a very strong magnet to see a dramatic change in the galvanometer.
equipment: Large Welch Galvanometer, Large Coil with Long Leads, Strong Magnet

title: Inductance With Sound
description: Tape Player Setup: Insert the audio jack into the Monitor jack on the cassette player. Connect the other end of the audio cable to the inner coil. Attach the speakers and the outer coil to the sound system. Press play on the cassette player and move the inner coil in and out of the outer coil to hear the music start and stop coming out of the speaker. Phone Setup: Insert the audio jack into the phone (with the dongle if necessary).Connect the other end of the audio cable to the inner coil. Attach the speakers and the outer coil to the sound system.Press play on thephoneand move the inner coil in and out of the outer coil to hear the music start and stop comingout of the speaker.
notes: For a quantitative understanding of the fluctuations in volume, use the analog decibel meter near the speakers. The amplifier pictured in the video is not necessary for the demonstration, since the speakers in the picture have been replaced with more powerful speakers. Both the white speaker and the amplifier are not present in the kit. The sound system can be loud enough such that the effect of moving the coils can be heard throughout a large classroom.

title: Pendulum in a Magnetic Field
description: This demonstration shows how eddy currents create an opposing magnet field. As the solid pendulum swings through the magnetic field, eddy currents are produced because of the changing magnetic flux in the aluminum. These currents create a magnetic field opposite of that of the magnet which slows the pendulum. The hollow pendulum does not slow as much because there is not as much area for the eddy currents. Therefore, is a smaller magnetic field to slow the pendulum. The pendulum with the slots does not easily allow for the movement of eddy currents and thus does not slow like the others. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the Horseshoe Magnet with Mounted Rod Apparatus and the three pendulums on the lab table. Hang one pendulum on the rod so that it will swing freely between the poles of the magnet.  Pull the pendulum back, release, and observe what happens.  Repeat this procedure with the other pendulums.
notes: None
equipment: Horseshoe Magnet Mounted with Rod Above, Three Aluminum Pendulums:SolidHollowSlits, Solid, Hollow, Slits

title: Ring Launch
description: This setup demonstrated electromagnetic induction with alternating current. The AC in the coil induces an opposite AC in the aluminum ring which creates opposite magnetic fields causing the ring to be repelled off the tower.  In the coil with light bulb, a current is induced in the coil which lights the bulb. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Purchased Setup - Larger Place the apparatus on the demo table. Place the ring, coil, or broken ring around the core.  Flip the switch.  The ring will launch. The bulb will light on the coil.  The broken ring will do nothing. Notre Dame Built Setup - Smaller Ensure the main power is off on the control box.  Twist the red and black banana cables together.  Connect the red terminal on the ring launcher to the red jack on the power control box using the red banana cable.  Connect the black terminal on the ring launcher to the black jack on the power control box using the black banana cable. Place one ring on top of the coil around the core.  Select one of the three power settings on the control box.  Turn the main power on the control box on and the ring will fly off.  Turn main power on the control box off.  Repeat this procedure with the ring with the slit and nothing will happen.
notes: Immerse the ring in liquid nitrogen to achieve a higher jump.
equipment: Ring Launch Coil with Core, Power Control box, One Red Banana Cable, One Black Banana Cable, One Solid Ring, One Ring with a Slit, Coil with Light Bulb

title: Simple Electric Motor
description: This demonstration shows a very simple conversion of electrical to mechanical energy.  This simple motor is made of a battery, piece of wire, and magnet.  All the materials can be easily found and the device assembled at home.  The wire has been wound into a coil and hung on a stand made of paper clips.  Once the battery is connected to system, the coil will spin because of the force from the magnetic field on the current in the coil. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the simple electric motor setup on the demo table.  Place the battery between the bent paper clips and the coil in the bent paper clip cradle.  Connect the battery to the setup using the banana cables and alligator clips. Spin the coil to start the motor.  The coil should spin rapidly. Disconnect the battery when finished.
notes: Be careful!  The magnet is strong and will easily jump.
equipment: Electric Motor Setup (cork board, bent paper clips, coil), Round Black Magnet, Two Banana Cables, Four Alligator Clips, D Battery in Holder

title: Radio Transmission
description: This demonstration shows the effect of a Faraday cage on a small portable radio. When placed inside the cage, the radio doesn’t receive signal and the transmission is blocked. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the radio on aluminum foil, turn it on and adjust the frequency until you reach any radio station. Place the cage above it and show that by doing so you lose signal.
notes: Coming Soon
equipment: Small Portable Radio, Aluminum Foil, Metallic cage

title: Tesla Coil
description: This demonstration shows what happens when a fluorescent light bulb is brought close to a tesla coil. The bulb lights up as it gets closer to the coil.
setup: Place the tesla coil on table. Make sure the knob has been turned counter-clockwise. Plug in the tesla coil and turn the knob clockwise until a buzzing sound is heard. Hold the fluorescent bulb (DO NOT TOUCH THE METAL ENDS) and slowly approach the coil (DO NOT TOUCH THE COIL WITH IT). It should light up (it might be helpful to turn the lights off).
notes: Coming Soon
equipment: Tesla Coil, Fluorescent Bulb

title: Charge Propelled Cylinder
description: A charged rod will induce charge separation and attract a neutral soda can causing it to roll. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the equipment on the lab table.Place the soda can on its' side so that it can roll.  Vigorously rub the fur on the rod to charge it.  Bring the rod near the can to cause it to roll. This can be done with the rod and silk or the balloon as well.
notes: None
equipment: Aluminum Can, Rubber Rod, Fur, Glass Rod, Silk, Balloon (optional)

title: Comb or Rod and Fur with Confetti
description: Running a comb through hair will negatively charge the comb. Doing this or negatively charging the rod with the fur then bringing it near confetti will attract the confetti. Because the confetti is so light, it can be pulled toward the charged rod or comb. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the equipment on the lab table.Run the comb through your hair to negatively charge it or rub the rod with the fur to negatively charge it. Bring the comb or rod near the confetti and see it attract.
notes: None
equipment: Comb, Rod, Fur, Small Pieces of Paper, Webcam

title: Electrophorus
description: The electrophorus is a device that can be electrostatically charged. The metal base plate will become strongly charged when rubbed with fur. If you now take a large disk-shaped metal plate with an insulating handle and place it on the plate, the face becomes positively charged by induction while the other side acquires the opposite charge. If the demonstrator now touches the back plate, thus conducting away the charge on the back, and then removes the plate by the handle, it will have a net positive charge. Bring this near an electroscope to show it is charged. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the equipment on the lab table.  Set up the webcam to view the electroscope.Remove the top plate with handle from the base.  Rub the fur on the base.  Replace the top plate using the handle.  Touch the back of the top plate.  Remove the top plate using the handle and it will be charged.  Bring it near the electroscope to demonstrate this.
notes: None
equipment: Electrophorus, Insulated Base Plate, Fur, Electroscope, Webcam

title: Pith Ball
description: A pith ball is a very light weight ball that is coated with a conducting material.  When a negatively charged rod is brought near the pith ball it will induce a charge in the pith ball and attract it.  Because the pith ball is so light you can easily see it being attracted to the rod.  If contact is made and electrons transferred, you can easily see the pith ball repelled from the charged rod. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Use the support rods and clamps to hang a pith ball from a string.  Connect the webcam to the projector system and set it up to view the pith ball. Rub the rod on the fur to charge the rod.  Bring the rod near the pith ball without touching it. Rub the rod on the fur to charge the rod.  Bring the rod near the pith ball and touch it.  Now bring the rod near the pith ball again. Touch the pith ball with your hand to ground it.
notes: None
equipment: 2 Support Rods, Right Angle Clamp, String, Pith Ball, Rubber Rod, Fur, Webcam

title: Rod with Fur or Silk and the Electroscope
description: This demonstration is used to show how an electroscope works, the types of charge, and types of charging. Rubbing the rod on the fur adds electrons to the rod giving it a negative charge. Using the the silk and rod, takes electrons from the rod giving the rod a positive charge. Touching the electroscope with a charged rod demonstrates charging by contact. To charge by induction, a charged rod is brought near the electroscope which is then grounded. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the rods, fur, silk, electroscope, and grounding wire on the lab table.  Setup the webcam to view the electroscope and connect it to the projector system.Negatively charge the rod by rubbing it on the fur.  Touch the electroscope to give it a negative charge. Positively charge the other rod by rubbing it on the silk.  Touch the electroscope to give it a positive charge. Charging the opposite rod and touching the electroscope once it is charged with reverse the effect. Touch the electroscope between examples to ground it. Bringing a charged rod near the electroscope without touching it, then connecting the grounding wire and grounding the electroscope will show charging by induction. Again, touch the electroscope to ground the system once finished.
notes: None
equipment: Electroscope, Teflon Rod, Nylon Rod, Fur, Silk, Grounding Cable, Webcam

title: Static Balloon
description: Rubbing a balloon on your hair (or fur) will electrostatically charge the balloon. It will stick to a wall as it induces a charge in the wall. You can also repel a hanging balloon with the charged balloon or attract small pieces of paper. Charging a rod and bringing it near these object will also produce attraction or repulsion. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place all the equipment on the lab table.  Hang a balloon from a ring stand. Rub the balloon on your hair or fur to negatively charge it.  Bring the charged balloon near the hanging balloon.  Bring the charged balloon near the small pieces of paper.  Touch the charged balloon to the wall and it will stick. Charging the rods and bringing them near these objects will also demonstrate attraction and repulsion.
notes: None
equipment: Balloons, String (to hang on from the ceiling), Rubber Rod, Glass Rod, Fur, Silk, Small Pieces of Paper, Ring Stand, Webcam

title: Static Electron Deflection of a Stream of Water
description: A negatively charged rod will attract a stream of water. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the equipment on the lab table.  If using the sink, setup the webcam to view it. Charge the rod using the fur.  Bring it near the stream of water and the water stream will deflect. This can also be done using the balloon or comb and your hair.
notes: Do not contact the water or your device will lose charge.
equipment: Stream of Water, Rubber Rod, Fur, Balloon (optional), Comb (optional), Webcam (optional)

title: Van de Graaff Generator
description: The Van de Graaff generator is a completely self-contained high voltage generator which operates on 105-125 volts AC or DC. The voltages present are harmless due to the very small current that can be drawn. In fact, the entire output of the machine may be safely discharged to the hand. Charge is scraped off the belt running up the tube in the center of the machine and distributed onto the metal sphere on top. The sphere will discharge and ground to nearby objects.  In order to prevent unexpected shocks, the sphere should always be discharged using the discharge sphere. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the equipment on the lab table.  Be sure to connect the discharge sphere.Plug in the Van de Graaff Generator and increase the motor speed using the dial on the front.  Bring the discharge sphere near the main sphere to see the sphere discharge. Once the machine is turned off, discharge the sphere again.
notes: Be careful to avoid unexpected shocks.

title: DC to AC
description: This demonstration shows how to convert DC to AC using an RLC circuit.  A battery is used to charge up the capacitor, then a switch is flipped and the circuit discharges showing damped AC.
setup: Set the whiteboard on the lab table. Connect the webcam to the projector and set it up to view the whiteboard from above. Using circuit scribe build the circuit shown above. Connect channel A of the pico scope across the capacitor and channel B of the pico scope across the inductor. Open the pico scope software and turn on channel B. Set both channels to 5V and DC. Choose 100 micro s per division and 100 kS. At the bottom of the screen, Trigger should be set to Auto. Turn on the battery and close the switch to charge the inductor (you should see a voltage).  Open the switch to see an AC voltage.  Hit Stop to view this.
notes: Be sure that all the grounds for the pico scope are connected at the same point as the ground for the function generator!
equipment: Circuit Scribe Kit, Whiteboard, Pico Scope, Two BNC to Banana Cables, Webcam, Demo Computer, Switch, 100 ohm Resistor, 4.7 micro Farad Capacitor, 1 H inductor

title: Ampere Balance
description: This demonstration shows the force between two parallelconductors carrying current. The currents can be set up to be parallel or anti-parallel to each other.
setup: Place the power supply on the lab table.  Connect both wires to the power supply.  Connect the wires to the apparatus either so that the currents on the conductors are parallel or antiparallel. Press the button on the power supply and release it.  The wires will attract or repel.
notes: The power supply is operated by a push button that must be held in to remain on. Do not leave the current on for too long or the wires will get hot.
equipment: High Current Power Supply, Long Banana Cable, Ampere Balance Apparatus

title: Force Between Parallel Wires
description: This demonstration shows the force between two parallel current carrying wires.  Two wires are setup next to each other.  When current passes through them it creates a magnetic field around them.  Depending on the direction of the current and thus the direction of the magnetic field, the wires will either attract or repel. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the power supply on the lab table.  Connect both wires to the power supply.  Connect the wires to the stand either so that the wires on the stand are parallel or antiparallel.  Connect the webcam to the projector system.  Set up the webcam to view the wires. Press the button on the power supply and release it.  The wires will attract or repel.
notes: Do not leave the current on or the wires will get hot.
equipment: High Current Power Supply, Two Long Banana Cables, Wooden Stand, Webcam

title: Jumping Wire
description: This demonstration shows the force on a current carrying wire in a permanent magnetic field.  A cable is draped into a magnetic field between the poles of a magnet.  When a current is run through the wire, it jumps due to the force. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the equipment on the lab table.  Plug the banana cable into the high current power supply.  Drape the cable over the magnet so that it falls between the two poles. Use the knob on the power supply to select the desired amount of current.  Press the red button the power supply to turn on the current and see the wire jump.
notes: The power supply is operated by a push button that must be held in to remain on. Do not leave the current on for too long or the wires will get hot.
equipment: High Current Power Supply, Long Banana Cable, Green Horseshoe Magnet

title: Lorentz Force (Crookes Tube)
description: This setup demonstrates the force of a magnetic field on moving electric charges. The Crookes tube creates a beam of electrons that is visible because of an inert gas in the tube. When a magnet is brought near the tube, the beam deflects from the magnetic force. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Setup the apparatus as shown in the photo.Setup the support rod on the lab table and attach the support platform to it (Note: If using a ring stand, consider securing it to the table with duct table or a c-clamp as the setup can be wobbly while being moved). Using the clamps, secure the Crookes Tube onto the support platform. Using two black banana cables, connect the " H " terminals on the Crookes Tube to the yellow AC jacks on the power supply (orientation does not matter).  Connect the red " P " terminal on the Crookes Tube to the red High Voltage jack on the power supply. Using the other black banana cable, connect the black " K " terminal on the Crookes Tube to the black " + 500 V " terminal on the power supply. Ensure that the apparatus is properly setup before turning it on.Turn the power supply knob down to ensure that the equipment starts at 0 V.  Turn off the lights in the room. Turn on the power supply.  Set DC to 300V and AC to 6V using the power supply.  It may take a moment for a blue-green beam to appear in the tube.  Bring the magnet near the tube to show the deflection.
notes: CAUTION: High Voltage.  Ensure that equipment is setup properly before use! May need to be performed in a darkened room in order to see the electron beam.
equipment: Pasco SF-9585A High Voltage Power Supply, Nakamura Crookes Tube, Support Rod or Ring Stand, Support Platform, 2 Clamps, 1 Red Banana Cable, 3 Black Banana Cables, Bar Magnet

title: Magnetic Field Around a Current Carrying Wire
description: This demonstration visually shows the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire. When the power supply is off and there is not current in the wire, all the compasses point in the same direction (north). When the power is turned on and current runs through the wire, the compasses reorient themselves to show the rings around the wire where the magnetic field is. The closer to the wire the stronger the field. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the equipment on the lab table.  Connect the platform with wire to the high current power supply using the high current cables.  Arrange the compasses around the straight wire on the platform.  Connect the webcam to the projector system and place it so it views the compasses around the wire. Turn the knob on the power supply to the desired current.  Press the power button on the power supply and hold it for a few seconds.  Watch the compasses realign around the wire.
notes: The power supply is operated by a push button that must be held in to remain on.  Do not leave the current on for too long or the wires will get hot.
equipment: High Current Power Supply, Two High Current Banana Cables, Clear Platform with Straight Wire Apparatus, Many Compasses, Webcam

title: Magnetic Field Around Various Currents
description: This demonstration visually shows the magnetic field around different currents.  Compasses are placed around a pair of coils and a toroid.  When a current through the coils is turned on, the compasses reorient to show the magnetic field.
setup: Place the equipment on the lab table.   Connect the desired platform with coil to the high current power supply using the high current cables. Arrange the compasses around the coil on the platform. Connect the webcam to the projector system and place it so it views the compasses around the wire. Turn the knob on the power supply to the desired current. Press the power button on the power supply and hold it for a few seconds. Watch the compasses realign around the coil.  Repeat this procedure for the other coil.
notes: The power supply is operated by a push button that must be held in to remain on. Do not leave the current on for too long or the wires will get hot.
equipment: High Current Power Supply, 4 High Current Banana Cables, Clear Platform with Pair of Coils Apparatus, Clear Platform with Toroid Apparatus, Many Compasses

title: Magnetic Force on an Electron Beam (Using e/m Apparatus)
description: The setup demonstrates the force of a magnetic field on moving electric charges. It consists of pair of Helmholtz coils surrounding a vacuum tube filled with an inert gas. As current passes through the coils, a uniform magnetic field is created between them. The vacuum tube contains an electron gun that produces a glowing beam as the gas atoms are excited by the moving electrons. As the current in the coils is increased, the beam is bent into a circle from the force of the magnetic field. A bar magnet can be used to further deflect the beam. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Connect the equipment as shown in the photo.The e/m apparatus should be located in the middle of the lab table with the Tenma power supply to the left and the Pasco power supply to the right (when looking at the front of the equipment).  Connect the " - " terminal on the Tenma power supply with a black banana cable to the black banana jack for the Helmholtz Coils (located one the left side of the e/m apparatus).  Connect the " + " terminal of the Tenma power supply to the red banana jack for the Helmholtz Coils using a red banana cable.  Using two black banana cables, connect the yellow jacks on the Pasco power supply to the black terminals for the heater (located on the far right side of the e/m apparatus; orientation does not matter).  Using a red banana cable, connect the High Voltage red terminal on the Pasco power supply to the red terminal for the electrodes (second column in on the right side of the e/m apparatus).  Use the last black banana cable to connect the black terminal for " + 500 V " on the Pasco power supply to the black terminal for the electrodes. Ensure the equipment is properly connected before turning it on.Turn the knobs on the supplies down so that everything is at zero to begin.  Turn off the lights in the room. Turn on the power supplies.  The Pasco power supply should be set at approximately 200-220 V for the electrodes.  It may take a moment for a blue-green beam to be visible.  Turn up the voltage on the Tenma power supply for the Helmholtz Coils to see the beam deflect into a circle.
notes: CAUTION: High Voltage.  Ensure that equipment is setup properly before use! Should be performed in a darkened room in order to see the electron beam. Instructors can use a bar magnet to further deflect the electron beam.
equipment: Tenma 0-18V DC Power Supply, Pasco SF-9585A High Voltage Power Supply, e/m Apparatus, 2 Red Banana Cables, 4 Black Banana Cables, 1 Power Cable, Bar Magnet (optional)

title: Torque on a Current Loop
description: This demonstration shows the torque on a current loop in a magnetic field.  When current runs through a loop that is in a magnetic field, a magnetic field is created which causes the loop to rotate.
setup: Place the apparatus on the lab table.  Connect the battery or power supply to the apparatus using the banana cables. Press the button on the power supply or touch the battery to turn on the current.  The loop will twitch or rotate in the magnetic field.
notes: None
equipment: Torque on a Current Loop Apparatus, Two Banana Cables, D Battery or High Current Power Supply

title: Diamagnetism - Levitating Magnet
description: Diamagnetic materials are those which repel both poles of a magnet.  This demonstration uses the diamagnetic material pyrolytic graphite to float a magnet.  The wood jig has two pyrolytic graphite plates.  When a magnet is placed between them, with a lifter magnet (to compensate for gravity) placed above.  The system can be adjusted so that the magnet floats in the air between the two plates. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the wood jig on the demo table.  Attach the lifter magnet to the adjustment screw.  Place the floater magnet between the graphite plates. Move the adjustment screw up or down until the magnet floats between the plates. The gap between the plates may be adjusted using the screw on the back of the jig as well. A camera may be used to view this demonstration as it is quite small.
notes: None
equipment: Wood Jig with Pyrolytic Graphite Plates, Lifter Magnet, Floater Magnet

title: Magnets Show and Tell
description: Magnets come in all different shapes and sizes.  This demo lets students see many shapes, sizes, and orientations of magnets.
setup: Place the magnets on the lab table.  Be sure to leave enough space between them that they do not get stuck together.
notes: Be careful not to get pinched between two magnets!
equipment: Various Magnets (Different Shapes and Sizes)

title: Meissner Effect
description: This demonstration shows the Meissner effect.  A superconductor in a petri dish is cooled using liquid nitrogen.  Once chilled, a small magnet may be suspended above the superconductor showing how the properties of the superconductor changed with temperature. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the petri dish on the demo table.  Put the superconducting disk in the center of the dish. Wearing gloves and safety goggles, pour the liquid nitrogen over the superconductor. Allow the system to sit until the top of the superconducting disk is no longer covered by liquid nitrogen. Using the tweezers carefully suspend the magnet over the superconductor.  If the magnet will not float, the system is not cold enough. This may also be done with the magnet sitting on the superconductor and the liquid nitrogen poured over the system.  Once the superconductor is cold enough, the magnet will raise up off the disk.
notes: Be careful when handling liquid nitrogen.  Be sure to use gloves and goggles.
equipment: Petri Dish, Superconducting Dish, Small Magnet, Plastic Tweezers, Goggles, Gloves, Liquid Nitrogen, Webcam, Stand

title: Rolling Magnets
description: This demonstration shows how magnets behave.  Collisions are compared between a non-magnetic ball and a magnetic ball hit several balls on a ramp.
setup: Place the ramp and balls on the lab table. Place the non-magnetic balls on the ramp.  Pull one back and release it to see how the balls react to the collision. Place one magnetic ball at the top of the ramp.  Release it to see how the balls react to the collision.
notes: None
equipment: Wood Ramp, Magnetic Balls, Steel Balls

title: Jacob's Ladder
description: This exciting demonstration can be used to show multiple concepts.  A step-up transformer creates a voltage that exceeds the dielectric breakdown of air between two rods.​  It can be used to discuss transformers, as well as general principles in electricity. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the Jacob's Ladder apparatus on the demonstration table.  Place the clear plastic safety shield over the device.Turn on the apparatus and the spark will rise up between the wires. CAUTION: LETHAL VOLTAGES.  UNPLUG THE DEVICE BEFORE MAKING ADJUSTMENTS.
notes: The wires may require some bending to get the best spark.  The wires should be straight and clean.
equipment: Jacob's Ladder Apparatus, Protective Plastic Shield for Jacob's Ladder

title: Types of Resistors
description: This demonstration shows the different types and sizes of resistors all mounted on one board.
setup: Place the Resistor Board on the demo table. The instructor can talk about the different types and sizes of resistors.
notes: None
equipment: Resistor Board

title: Bernoulli's Principle - Bag
description: This demonstration shows how you can easily fill up a large bag using Bernoulli's principle.  If you blow into the bag from a small distance away from the opening, the bag will easily fill.  This is because the air you blow into the bag has a greater velocity than the air around it, which creates a drop in pressure, causing outside air to rush into the bag. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the Bernoulli Bag on lab table.  Tie one end. As demonstrated in the video, blow into the bag from a distance away and the bag will quickly fill up.
notes: The demonstration may require some practice ahead of time.
equipment: Large Bernoulli Bag

title: Bernoulli's Principle - Floating Ball
description: Brief Description * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.

title: Tornado Vortex
description: This demonstration shows turbulence and how a vortex is formed.  As the water drains from the top bottle to the bottom one, the system is spun which creates the vortex. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the apparatus on the lab table. With one 2 L bottle full of water and one not, flip the apparatus over so the water filled bottle is on top and give it a spin. The water should begin to form a vortex in the top bottle as the water spills down. Note, the faster the water spins, the larger the vortex becomes.​
notes: None
equipment: Two 2 L Bottles, Tornado Connector, Water, Colored Lamp Oil (Optional)

title: Venturi Tubes
description: This demonstration shows Bernoulli's Principle.  The bottom of the tubes are filled with colored water and air is blown through.  Because of the shape of the tube, the air moves faster through the center causing a lower pressure.  Therefore, the water in the center tube is pulled higher. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Mount the Venturi tubes using the stands and clamps.  Place the white board behind so that the colored water will be more visible. Fill the bottom of the apparatus with colored water. Attach the tube to the air supply. Turn on the air and watch the water levels change.
notes: None
equipment: Venturi Tubes Apparatus, Colored Water, Air Source (in lecture hall), Stands  and Clamps, White Board, Webcam (optional)

title: Archimedes Principle
description: More Information Coming Soon. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Coming Soon
notes: Coming Soon

title: Equilibrium Tubes
description: Despite the different shapes of the tubes in this vessel, the water level will be the same when filled.  This is due to the atmospheric pressure. * Equipment seen in the photo may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Using the burette clamp and stand, setup the glass tube apparatus so that is securely sitting upright. Mix food coloring with water in the beaker. Pour the water into the tube apparatus.  The level of the water will be even despite the very different shapes of the tubes.
notes: None
discussion_questions: Why is the water level the same in each column? | What would happen if the pressure in one column was increased and the others were still open?
