title: Sunset Demonstration
description: This demonstration shows why sunsets appear red in the sky.  As the sun sets, it is lower in the sky and thus the white light from it has to travel through more of the atmosphere before it reaches our eyes.  The light encounters more particles in the atmosphere so more of the higher frequency, shorter wavelength light is scattered away.  This leaves the lower frequency, longer wavelength red light to reach our eyes. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the fish tank on the demo table.  Place the lamp on a board on one end and the white screen on the other end of the tank.  Place the lens between the tank and the lamp. Turn on the lamp and adjust the height of the lens and screen so that the light passes through the lens and the tank, and is visible on the screen.  Turn off the lamp. Fill the tank with water so that the entire light beam passes through the water. In the beaker, mix coffee creamer with water until there are no chunks. Turn on the lamp and slowly add the creamer mixture to the tank.  Stir to combine.  Repeat this process, watching as the image on the screen turns yellow, then orange, then red.  Eventually the light will not be able to pass through the tank.
notes: This is best done with the lights down or off. This can also be done with Pine Sol but the correct ratio is more difficult to get.
equipment: Fish Tank, Water, Coffee Creamer, 250 W Lamp Sitting on Board to Raise the Height, 500 mm Lens with Stand, White Screen, Beaker, Wooden Spoon

title: Fiber Optics

These are many little strands of Plexiglas (each a tiny light pipe) that are connected together in a flexible bundle.  Shine the laser through one end of the bundle  you can see that most of the light comes out of the other end of the bundle. You may also see the light leakage at the kinks in the strands. ​ *Image Coming Soon*
setup: Place the equipment on the lab table.  If requested, setup the webcam with the projector to view the system. Shine the laser through one end of the fiber optic bundle.  The other end of the bundle will light up.  There should be minimal light leaked along the way.
notes: Be careful not to point the laser at anyone or look directly into the beam. May need to be performed in a darkened room.
equipment: Fiber Optic Bundle, Laser, Webcam (optional)

notes: Be careful, the lamp gets warm.

title: Refraction Tank
description: The refraction tank shows how light is reflected and refracted when traveling from air to water.  The rotating light source allows you to change the angle of incidence and the scale on the apparatus allows for measuring the angle of reflection and refraction.  This can be used to study Snell's Law.  Total Internal Reflection can also be seen at the appropriate angle. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Set the apparatus on the lab table.  Fill the tank halfway (up to the 90oline) with water.  Connect the power supply.  Connect the webcam to the projector system.  Setup the webcam to view the tank. Turn on the light source and rotate it to see different angles.  This can be used to calculate Snell's Law or view Total Internal Reflection.
notes: None
equipment: Refraction Tank, Refraction Tank Power Supply, Distilled Water, Webcam

title: Water Cup Rainbow
description: This demonstration shows refraction and reflection in a water cup.  As white light enters the water, it is refracted which separates the colors.  It is then reflected off the back of the cup.  As this light exits the cup into the air, it is again refracted separating the colors further and creating a rainbow.
setup: Set up a white screen on the demo table and behind it. Place the lamp in stand with power supply on the screen.  Place the water cup in front of the lamp. Turn on the lamp and adjust the cup so that a rainbow forms on the screen behind it.
notes: The rainbow is more easily visible with the lights off. Be careful, the lamp gets warm after prolonged use.
equipment: Two White Screens, Short Stand, Right Angle Clamp, Burette Clamp, Lamp with Power Supply, Cup Filled with Water

title: Water Drop Rainbow
description: This demonstration simulates light passing through a water droplet.  As the white light enters the drop it is refracted which separates the colors.  It is then reflected off the other surface of the drop.  From there the light passes through the drop, then leaves the drop entering the air.  This again causes refraction which separates the colors even further into a visible rainbow.
setup: Set up a white screen on the demo table and behind it. Place the lamp in stand with power supply on the screen.  Place the round bottom flask filled with water in front of the lamp. Turn on the lamp and adjust the flask so that a rainbow appears on the screen behind it.
notes: The rainbow is most prominent with the room lights off. Be careful, the lamp gets warm after prolonged use.
equipment: Two White Screens, Short Stand, Right Angle Clamp, Burette Clamp, Lamp with Power Supply, Round Bottom Flask Filled with Water

notes: This may work better in a darkened room.

title: Polarization by Scattering
description: This demonstration shows polarization by scattering.  Light is projected up through a beaker filled with water mixed with coffee creamer.  A polarizer is held in front of the beaker.  As the polarizer is rotated, the beaker appears brighter and dimmer showing that the light is now polarized. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations. Pour the mixture into the other beaker and stir until combined. Turn on the lamp and dim the lights in the room. Hold a polarizer in front of the beaker and rotate it to see the brightness change.
notes: This may be done with a simple lamp as well.

title: Rubens Tube
description: This demonstration shows acoustic standing waves.  The apparatus is a long aluminum tube with holes in it.  A speaker is attached at one end. setup: Place the Rubens tube apparatus on two lab tables pushed together.  (It is too long for one lab table.) Attach the hose to the Rubens tube and the gas supply. Attach the function generator or music source to the power amplifier and the power amplifier to the speaker using banana cables. Turn on the gas supply and wait a few seconds.  Light the gas escaping from the holes.Make sure all the holes are lit.Adjust the gas supply so that flames are a few inches long.  Too little gas and the flames will easily go out.  Too much gas and the waves can be difficult to see. Turn on the sound and adjust the volume so that waves are visible.  If the sound is too loud, the flames will go out.  If the sound is too soft, the wave will not be visible. Once you are done, turn off the gas and the flames will go out.  Evacuate the tube with air if possible. Be careful, the tube will be hot.
notes: The classroom gas lines may need to be turned on using the knob underneath the sink.
discussion_questions: Rubens Tube Apparatus with Connection Hose | Power Amplifier | 2 - 4 Banana Cables | Function Generator | Gas Source | Lighter | Computer or Phone with Music (Optional) and Hook-Up Cable

title: Slinky Waves
description: Slinky's can be used to demonstrate longitudinal and transverse waves as well as wave pulses and wave interference.  There are several slinky's available so this demonstration may be done by the instructor or interactively by the students (depending on the class size). * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the slinky's on the lab table. Create the different type of waves by shaking the slinky parallel (longitudinal) or perpendicular (transverse) to it. Send multiple waves to see interference or standing waves.  This may need an additional volunteer.
notes: None
equipment: Slinkys

title: Standing Waves
description: This demonstration shows transverse standing waves in a string.  By oscillating a string at different frequencies, one can view standing waves and different harmonics. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Attach the posts to the demo table.  Mount the pulley and string vibrator to the posts. Stretch the spring over the pulley and attach it to the clamp or hanging mass. Connect the string vibrator to the sine wave generator using the banana cables. Starting with the amplitude all the way down, turn on the sine wave generator.  Turn down the frequency to the 15 Hertz range.  Increase the amplitude and adjust it as necessary to see different standing waves.
notes: Do not turn the amplitude up too high as it is bad for the equipment.  (You will hear clicking noises when this happens.)
equipment: Pasco Sine Wave Generator with Power Cables, Pasco String Vibrator, Stretchy String, Two Banana Cables, Pulley, Two Posts, Swivel Clamp, Hanging Mass (Depending on Setup)

title: Sympathetic Resonance - Tuning Forks
description: This demonstration shows how energy is carried in waves by demonstrating sympathetic resonance.  Two tuning forks of the same resonant frequency are placed on the table.  One is struck then dampened.  You can faintly hear the other one resonating. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the tuning forks and hammer on the lab table. Strike one of the tuning forks.  Touch the tuning fork to dampen it.  You should faintly hear the second tuning fork.
notes: None
equipment: Two Tuning Forks of the Same Frequency (the small ones work best, see picture), Tuning Fork Hammer

title: Tuning Fork Beats
description: This demonstrates beats between similar frequencies.  After striking the tuning forks, you can hear the beats created. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the tuning forks, dense putty, and mallet on the demo table. Position some putty on one of the tuning forks, close to the top. Strike both tuning forks with the mallet to hear the beats.  (You may need to adjust the position to make the beats more recognizable.) Adding more or less putty will change the frequency.
notes: None
equipment: Tuning Forks with Resonance Boxes, Adjustment Clamp, Mallet

title: Wave Addition (Beads Box)
description: This demonstration shows wave addition and interference.  Beads and straws are arranged in a sine wave.  As the black sine wave is slid in from the side of the box, the wave addition can be seen.
setup: Place the apparatus on the table. Slide the black wave pattern into the box to observe the wave interference.
notes: None
equipment: Beads Box Apparatus

title: Wave Machine
description: This apparatus demonstrates wave motion including standing waves and wave pulses.  Multiple pulses or standing waves can be shown.  There are multiple setups with different length rods as well. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the wave machine on the table. Lift the rods and lock the system in place. Move one end of the machine to send a pulse.  This can be done again to show interference or continued to show standing waves.
notes: None
equipment: Wave Machine Apparatus

title: Waves on a String
description: This demonstration shows transverse standing waves in a string.  By oscillating a string at different frequencies, one can view standing waves and different harmonics. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the waves on a string apparatus on the lab table. Connect the function generator to the apparatus using the banana cables. Adjust the frequency and amplitude until standing waves appear.
notes: None
equipment: Waves on a String Apparatus, Two Banana Cables, Function Generator

title: Boil Water in a Vacuum
description: This demonstration shows how you can boil water because of reduced pressure without a change in temperature. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place a small amount of water in a Pyrex beaker.  (Do not use a lot of water as this will take longer and can be damaging to the vacuum pump.) Place the beaker with water on the vacuum cart under the glass dome. Turn on the pump to evacuate the chamber. Once the pressure is low enough, the water will appear to boil despite no change in the temperature.
notes: Do not use a lot of water or leave the pump on for an extended period as the humidity is bad for the vacuum pump. Water will boil until it freezes after 10-15 minutes. Use a small watch glass to minimize heat absorption. Pump oil may need to be changed to reduce moisture in the system for this to occur. Use a thermometer to illustrate water temperature decreasing as it boils.
equipment: Vacuum Pump Cart, Glass Dome, Pyrex Beaker, Water

title: Drinking Bird
description: The Notre Dame Drinking Bird is a little different from the traditional Drinking Bird apparatus.  A heat lamp is placed below the bird so it acts like a palm glass.  As the liquid is heated, the vapor pressure pushes it toward the bird's head.  Once enough liquid reaches the head, the bird tips.
setup: Place the drinking bird apparatus on the demo table and plug it in. As the liquid heats, the bird will tip.
notes: None
equipment: Drinking Bird Apparatus

title: Palm Glass
description: This simple demonstration shows vapor pressure.  Holding one bulb in your hand increases the temperature and thus the vapor pressure.  This forces the liquid into the other bulb and causes it to appear to boil. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the palm glass apparatus on the demo table. Grab one bulb with your hand.  Observe the liquid.
notes: None
equipment: Palm Glass, Webcam (Optional)

title: PVT Surface
description: These PVT Surfaces can be used to discuss the change of state of elements based on pressure, volume, and temperature.  If any two of these is known, the third can be determined.  This creates the surface.
setup: Place the PVT Surface on the demo table. Use the PVT Surface to discuss the change of state based on pressure, volume, and temperature.
notes: None
equipment: PVT Surface

title: Thermal Oscillator
description: This apparatus demonstrates vapor pressure.  The lamp heats the lower bulb increasing the vapor pressure and forcing the liquid into the other bulb.  Once enough liquid enters the upper bulb, the apparatus tips and the process begins again.
setup: Place the apparatus onto the demo table. Plug the banana plugs into the first and third holes on the power supply. Plug in the power supply to turn on the lamp and start the process.
notes: None
equipment: Thermal Oscillator Apparatus, Gray Transformer Power Supply

title: Wet and Dry Bulb Hygrometer
description: This demonstration shows how two thermometers can be used to calculate the relative humidity.  One thermometer has a wet cloth over it; the other is dry.  The device is whirled in the air and then the temperature of each thermometer is read.  As the device is spinning, the water on the cloth is evaporating.  Using the difference between the temperatures and the table below, the relative humidity is calculated. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the device and a beaker of water on the demo table. Wet the cloth and wrap it around one of the thermometer bulbs. Whirl the device around your head for a few seconds. Measure and record the temperatures of the two bulbs.  Usethis tableto calculate the relative humidity.
notes: None
equipment: Hygrometer, Beaker of Water, Relative Humidity Table

title: Stirling Engine
description: This Stirling Engine converts heat energy to do mechanical work.  A wick soaked in alcohol is lit under a cylinder in the engine.  This heats the air in the cylinder.  After a few minutes, one of the wheels can be turned to start the engine running.  The cyclical expansion and compression of the air at different temperatures in different cylinders keeps the engine running. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the Stirling Engine on the demo table away from any other objects. Carefully fill the fuel cell with denatured alcohol so that it is no more than half full. Adjust the wick to 1/4" in length and place it and the cap on the fuel cell. Light the wick and wait several minutes for the engine to warm up. Turn one of the wheels to kick start the engine.  When hot enough, it should continue to run.
notes: Caution: this unit become very hot. Keep away from other objects and people.
equipment: Stirling Engine Apparatus, Denatured Alcohol

title: Constant Volume Bulb
description: This demonstration shows pressure vs. temperature in a gas at a fixed volume.  The bulb is placed in different temperature liquids to observe the change in pressure. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the constant volume bulb and beakers of fluids on the demo table. With the valve on the apparatus closed, place the bulb in the different fluids and observe the pressure change.
notes: If temperature and pressure values are recorded, absolute zero can be determined.
equipment: Constant Volume Bulb Apparatus, Beaker of Water, Beaker of Ice Water, Beaker of Hot Water, Thermometer, Liquid Nitrogen (Optional)

title: Balloon and Flame
description: The demonstration shows heat capacity.  A balloon filled with air will pop when heated, but a balloon filled with water will not. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Blow up one balloon. Blow up another balloon and partially fill with it water. Hold the flame below the balloon and it will pop. Hold the flame below the balloon with water in it and it will not pop.
notes: Be careful to keep the flame in the center of the water for best results.
equipment: Balloons, Lighter or Matches, Water

title: Ice Melting Blocks
description: This demonstration shows heat transfer, thermal conductivity, and change of state.  The two blocks are made of different material.  One is aluminum, the other is a high density foam.  To the touch, the aluminum feels cooler.  When an ice cube is placed on each, the cube on the aluminum block melts faster. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the two blocks on the demo table with the o-rings on top of them. Place an ice cube on each block to observe which melts faster.
notes: None
equipment: Ice Melting Blocks, Ice Cubes

title: Mechanical Equivalent of Heat
description: This demonstration shows the conversion of mechanical energy into thermal energy.   As the crank is turned, the mass is lifted but hovers over the ground as the rope slips.  This heats the drum due to friction.  A thermometer records the change in temperature.
setup: Clamp the apparatus to the demo table. Wrap the string attached to the mass around the drum and stretch the rubber band over the cork. Set up the doc cam to view the thermometer. Turn the crank and watch the temperature increase.
notes: The mass is very heavy.  Be careful not to drop it.
equipment: Mechanical Equivalent of Heat Apparatus, Mass, Rubber Band, Clamps, Doc Cam

title: Bimetallic Strip
description: This demonstration shows solid expansion and how different materials react to changes in temperature.  The strip is made of one side brass and one side steel bonded together.  As the strip is heated, it will curve towards the steel side because it expands less.  If the strip is cooled, it will bend the opposite way.  This shows the different expansion coefficients. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the strip and heat gun on the demo table. Use the heat gun to heat the strip and watch it curve. The strip may be dipped in liquid nitrogen to see it curve the opposite direction.
notes: Be careful as the metal will get hot.
equipment: Bimetallic Strip, Heat Gun or Bunsen Burner, Liquid Nitrogen (Optional)

title: Nichrome Wire
description: This demonstration shows the heating effects of current.  As more current is passed through the wire it sags, then glows.  This can also be used to talk about how a light bulb works. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the stands on the demo table.  Attach the alligator clips to the stands with the right angle clamps.  Make sure none to clamp at the insulated portion.  Do not let the metal touch. Cut a piece of Nichrome wire and suspend it between the alligator clips. Plug the adapter into the variac. Turn on the variac and slowly turn up the power.  The wire will bend, then glow.  Do not turn the power up too high or the wire will break.
notes: Be careful to the Nichrome wire doesn't touch any part of the stand system. Do not touch the wire while on as it will be very hot.
equipment: Two Stands, Two Right Angle Clamps, Plug to Alligator Adapter, Variac, Nichrome Wire

title: Ring and Ball
description: This demonstration shows thermal expansion in solids.  At room temperature, the ball fits through the ring.  When the ball is heated, it will not pass through the ring.  If both are heated, the ball will pass through the ring. * Equipment seen in the video may vary from equipment used in ND Demonstrations.  See information and images below for ND equipment and setup.
setup: Place the ball, ring, and heat gun on the demo table. Use the heat gun to heat the ball, or both the ball and the ring.
notes: Be careful, the metal will be hot.
equipment: Ball, Ring, Heat Gun or Bunsen Burner
